topic: understanding the concept of the sine, cosine, and tangent ratios (basic trigonometry)

easy.text: In a right triangle, the sine of an angle is defined as:

options.text: The length of the opposite side divided by the length of the hypotenuse
options.feedback: Correct -- sine (SOH from SOH-CAH-TOA) is Opposite over Hypotenuse.

options.text: The length of the adjacent side divided by the length of the hypotenuse
The length of the opposite side divided by the length of the adjacent side
The length of the hypotenuse divided by the length of the opposite side
options.feedback: This is the reciprocal of the sine ratio (cosecant), not sine itself.

medium.text: In a right triangle, the side opposite a given angle is 6, and the hypotenuse is 10. What is the sine of that angle?

options.feedback: This results from dividing hypotenuse by opposite (10/6), which is the reciprocal of sine, not sine itself.
This is just the opposite side length alone, without dividing by the hypotenuse as the sine ratio requires.
This is just the hypotenuse length alone, without applying the sine ratio calculation.

hard.text: A right triangle has a hypotenuse of 13 and one leg (adjacent to angle θ) of length 5. Using the Pythagorean theorem to find the missing leg (opposite to θ), what is tan(θ)?

options.feedback: Correct -- the missing leg is √(13²-5²)=√(169-25)=√144=12, so tan(θ) = opposite/adjacent = 12/5 = 2.4.
This inverts the correct ratio -- tangent is opposite over adjacent (12/5), not adjacent over opposite.
This is actually the cosine of θ (adjacent/hypotenuse), not the tangent.
This is actually the sine of θ (opposite/hypotenuse), not the tangent.

easy.hard: This ratio relates the side facing away from the angle to the triangle's longest side, opposite the right angle.
easy.medium: This ratio compares the side across from the angle to the longest side of the triangle.
easy.easy: This ratio is the side across from the angle, divided by the longest side.

medium.hard: Substitute the given opposite and hypotenuse lengths directly into the sine ratio definition.
medium.medium: Divide the opposite side length by the hypotenuse length.

hard.hard: First apply the Pythagorean theorem to solve for the missing leg length, then substitute both legs into the tangent ratio definition (opposite over adjacent).
hard.medium: First find the missing leg using a²+b²=c² (13²-5²), then divide that result by 5 for the tangent.
hard.easy: First find the missing side: √(169-25)=12. Then tan(θ)=12/5.
